title: mlflow.genai.review_queues on Databricks: guard each public fluent function with databricks_api_disabled so calls raise INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE instead of a 500 from OSS routes
answers: Why does list_review_queues or create_review_queue fail with INTERNAL_ERROR: Not Found on my Databricks workspace?
How do I make a new review queue fluent API raise a clear error on a Databricks tracking URI?
Where is the Databricks guard for review queue functions like set_review_queue_item_status or add_items_to_review_queue handled?
How do the label schema and review queue Databricks guardrails stay consistent?
body:
Path: mlflow/genai/review_queues/__init__.py handles the public fluent calls (create/get/list/update/delete review queues, queue items, item status) that route through TracingClient to the OSS tracking routes /api/3.0/mlflow/review-queues/*. On a Databricks tracking URI these routes are not implemented, so the guard is the chokepoint.
Rule: Decorate every public review_queues function with @databricks_api_disabled("<function_name>", _REVIEWS_UI_ALTERNATIVE), placed under @experimental, so it fails before any client or network work. _REVIEWS_UI_ALTERNATIVE = "Use the workspace Reviews UI." is the shared guidance string. Same pattern as the mlflow.genai.label_schemas guardrail.
Symptom: On a Databricks workspace, list_review_queues and create_review_queue returned a generic RestException: INTERNAL_ERROR: Not Found (HTTP 500), which looked like a server outage and gave the user no next step.
Constraints: Applies to the fluent functions in mlflow/genai/review_queues/__init__.py only. The guard fires regardless of whether the workspace has Review Queues preview enabled. Non-Databricks tracking URIs are unaffected. The function name in the decorator must match the function name, since the error message embeds it. Tests in tests/genai/review_queues/test_review_queues_sdk.py parametrize over both "databricks" and "databricks://profile" and assert no client init.
applies: Any new or existing public mlflow.genai.review_queues function that calls TracingClient review-queue methods, when the tracking URI is Databricks.
says: Creating or listing review queues in the cloud workspace fails with an internal server error.
Review queue operations crash with an internal failure instead of pointing to the interface.
Calling review queue commands against the managed workspace returns a confusing server error.
Guide users to the workspace reviews screen when programmatic review queues are unsupported.
search: Public fluent functions in mlflow/genai/review_queues/__init__.py must be decorated with @databricks_api_disabled directing users to 'Use the workspace Reviews UI.' when a Databricks tracking URI is configured. This decorator raises INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE before invoking TracingClient, preventing generic RestException: INTERNAL_ERROR: Not Found HTTP 500 errors caused by unimplemented routes on Databricks workspaces. The guard applies specifically to fluent review queue SDK functions and leaves non-Databricks tracking URIs unaffected.
